messages:
maya: FYI - FinTechCo is seeing a sustained stream of 429s from our API for the last ~45m. They say traffic is steady (no recent deploy). I pulled a few sample responses; headers look like: 

`HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests`
`x-rli-rpm-limit: 600`
`x-rli-rpm-remaining: 0`
`x-rli-tpm-limit: 10000`
`x-rli-tpm-remaining: 8342`
`Retry-After: 30`

They have multiple workers hitting the API in parallel (mobile + server). Asking for immediate help and whether we can temporarily raise RPM for their key while we investigate. Tagging infra/sre for root cause.

maya: attaching a small extract of their request pattern from our logs (anonymized):
```
# normalized log snippet
2026-02-18T18:02:11Z key=acct_XXX route=/v1/chat req_id=abc123 latency=120ms tokens_out=300 model=redwood-2
2026-02-18T18:02:11Z key=acct_XXX route=/v1/chat req_id=abc124 latency=134ms tokens_out=310 model=redwood-2
2026-02-18T18:02:12Z key=acct_XXX route=/v1/embeddings req_id=abc125 latency=45ms tokens_out=0 model=text-embed-1
2026-02-18T18:02:12Z key=acct_XXX route=/v1/chat req_id=abc126 latency=118ms tokens_out=290 model=redwood-2
```

maya: primary question - RPM is hitting zero remaining frequently but TPM is fine. Is this expected if they have bursty concurrency? What suggestions for customer and what short-term mitigation can we offer?

diego: Looking. Quick notes: RPM is per-minute token bucket. If they have a lot of short concurrent requests, the RPM bucket can empty quickly even if TPM is not near limit. Also we rate-limit at API key level for RPM and token-level for TPM differently.

diego: Can you paste a couple of full raw request timestamps and client-side concurrency numbers from FinTechCo (how many parallel workers / threads)? That will help us repro.

maya: Their engineer responded: "server pool of 12 workers making ~8 reqs/s total, mobile ~30 users each firing background requests but staggered. No exponential backoff, immediate retry loop on 429s every 5s." They also said they have a nightly batch that syncs leads (bursts every 10m).

sofia: If they retry aggressively on 429 with constant interval, that makes RPM worse (retry amplification). We should advise exponential backoff + jitter and to respect Retry-After. Also we can see if their SDK is misconfigured to fan-out duplicate requests.

samir: On repro steps: I can simulate 12 workers with a simple script locally and hit their API key (we have a test key) to see when RPM depletes. Proposed script snippet:
```
# bash - simulate N concurrent workers hitting /v1/chat at ~8rps total
for i in {1..12}; do while true; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer TESTKEY" -d '\{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":10\}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat > /dev/null & sleep 0.12; done & done
```

samir: I'll run this against staging to reproduce token-bucket exhaustion.

diego: Also check client side for pooling. If their server opens a lot of short-lived TCP connections, upstream proxies might be miscounting concurrency and creating spikes. Ask them for a pcap or metrics from their LB.

maya: I created a short-term support ticket to raise RPM by 2x for 2 hours pending remediation. quota-bot: can you confirm ticket/automated policy?

quota-bot: Ticket #Q-44521 created by maya — temporary RPM bump from 600 to 1200 for key acct_XXX, expires in 120 minutes. Automated audit log appended.

sofia: Good immediate move. Two follow-ups: 1) recommend client moves heavy background syncs to backoff windows and 2) implement client-side rate-limiter (token-bucket or leaky-bucket) so they don't exceed per-minute peaks even if TPM is fine.

maya: Suggested message to customer (copy): "We've temporarily increased the per-minute throttle for your API key for two hours while you roll out retries/backoff. Please implement exponential backoff with jitter and respect Retry-After headers. If you need a longer bump, we'll need an ETA on your fix and expected steady-state concurrency so we can size. Also consider batching small requests where possible."

samir: Results from my staging run: With 12 workers at ~8rps we hit `x-rli-rpm-remaining: 0` in about 35s. Server-side logs show the token bucket exhausted and subsequent requests received 429 with Retry-After ~28-32s. With exponential backoff 2^n * 100ms + jitter, retries drop by ~70% and bucket recovers.

diego: Important note: We also have a per-route short-term burst window that allows brief exceed up to 150% for a few seconds. If workload is sustained beyond that, the steady-state RPM takes over. So short spikes may pass, sustained fanout won't.

sofia: For internal follow-up: Can infra add per-key recent-minute charts to the console (current/minute avg, peak concurrency, retry rate) — helps diagnosing these customer escalations faster. Filed infra request IR-1987.

maya: Customer replied to say the temporary bump helped, 429s stopped for the duration. They plan to roll out client backoff tonight. They asked whether we can add a header to responses with `x-rli-retry-suggest` or more granular per-second guidance.

diego: We already expose `Retry-After` and the RPM/TPM headers. Adding per-second guidance is tricky because our throttling is minute-granular. We could add `x-rli-suggested-rps` calculated from `x-rli-rpm-remaining/60` but it might be noisy. If you want I can prototype in a week.

sofia: Short checklist for support reply to customer: 1) Keep the temp RPM bump for now; 2) Deploy exponential backoff + jitter on retries; 3) Respect Retry-After; 4) Reduce concurrent workers or add local client-side token bucket; 5) Move heavy batches to off-peak windows or batch payloads; 6) Share expected steady-state concurrency if they want a permanent quota change.

maya: I'll send that and close ticket after they confirm rollout. Also leaving a note for product: consider guidance docs for "Handling per-minute throttles (RPM) vs per-hour/day (TPM)" — customers often confuse the two.

samir: One more reproducible tip for engineers: when trying to repro a 429 that reports RPM==0, check both token counts and wall-clock grouping. The same number of tokens spread unevenly across the minute will produce very different experiences. Small script to plot per-second request counts helped me visualize the problem.

maya: Thanks all — let's follow up if the issue recurs after their client changes. :thumbsup:
